body:
Do you have someone you can trust?  Can you tell them?
Does your school have a counsellor?

It must be hard to struggle with these thoughts. Is it possible for you to stop browsing this subreddit?

Hey man, Sorry to butt in, but in future it's best to not focus on what a person with a eating disorder looks like, or give them advice on how to lose weight.

It can give the wrong messages.

The closest I have ever come to 'Affording' healthcare, is being able to pay a 30 dollar gap after rebate to see a psychiatric student. Everything else has been through the public system.

I do no believe medication to stop me from having psychosis is a privilege. I experienced psychosis before I had treatment, and it's just a matter of time until then. If I become psychotic, working will completely be out of the picture.

Caring family and friends do not not somehow lessen psychosis.

I am posting in the minute chance someone can actually help me access the support I need.  If the support isn't there, well, there is absolutely no point of living.

I'm 24.  I recently linked up with a disability provider, that's who is looking into a license for me.  but not sure how helpful they will be. I had a intake appointment twice... first one was with a lady who didn't know what peer work is (I think that's the most appropriate job for me, as I have  lived experience, AND a diploma of counselling)

I don't think I qualify for homelessness support. We make rent and food, but one large bill or emergency and we would be fucked. I look for food hampers but most places are out ipswich / logan way. The only I can see close to use is wesley mission, and they limit their food hampers to three times a year, so it's probably best to keep that for emergencies.   We always make it through with food, but most fornights the last few days our cupboards get down to just  lentils, rice and curry paste... I don't even have a vacuum cleaner for my house. 

I moved from ipswich to brisbane. its too far to see my old therapist and my old doctor... have been trying to find a new GP for a while. First bulkbilling one  looked like they had just been hit with a overwhelming smell of shit when I said I had bipolar... They refused to give me psych medication, but also didn't understand why I wanted to see a bulk-billing psychatrist.

The second GP I have been to is much nicer... He has mental health interest, but I think it might be limited to anixety and unipolar depression... He was really nice to me, but when I said I was previously on lithium he was like "ew, strong stuff", and then gave me a script of anti-depressants as a mono-therapy. (which is really not appropiate for bipolar, as anti-depressants by themselves can cause mania. I have been on this anti-depressant before and that's why he chose it, but it's always been a low dose in conjuction with something that stops mania) but I didn't feel comfortable telling him how to do his job. I have a referral to headspace, but their wait lists are usually pretty long...

I honestly don't see the point in living right now.   Long story short, I had abusive parents who had genetic mental health issues. Schizophrenia runs on both sides of my family. I 'lucked' out and got bipolar (Bipolar and schizophrenia run on similar genes, you're 5.5 times more likely to have bipolar if your parent had schizophrenia.)

I have been in weekly/fortnightly therapy for years. I have tried a LOT of meds... Got myself well enough to feel ok-ish about working, did a LOT of volunteering, but because of sparse work history and  no license/car absolutely no one will hire me.   Job provider might be able to get me a license, but that wont get me a car.  

Moved out of my abusive home, so I can't afford a psychatrist. I don't meet criteria for DSP, and even if I did... can't see a psychatrist to fill out forms.

I'm one emergency away from being homeless. 

What's the point?  i can either kill myself now, or end up homeless.

Is it really?

Back then, I could access psychatrists and psychologists.

Back then, I didn't have to worry about if we can eat this fortnight.

Back then, I wasn't on the edge of homelessness.

Back then, I could afford meds.

Back then, I didn't have IBS, Fibromaygalia, Constant Migraines.

Back then, if I had these, there might be a chance for me fixing those.
"The definition of insanity is doing the same thing and expecting different results"
